Implementation Plan

Implementation plan for issue: E2E smoke canary B (run 39879064171)

Planning ref: `orchestrator/project-7905` at `e5537d8f92c4ec7e2c44a8c015b005841f315295`. The integration branch mismatch line reads `false`, so there is no mismatch. I did not check whether the target file already exists on this ref. The plan covers both cases.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends tests/e2e_smoke_canary_b.txt
Scope-mode justification: The issue spells out one data file and its exact contents. No helper, script or workflow is involved, so the plan changes nothing outside that file. It follows the issue as written and does not expand or reduce it.

What the plan changes: it only edits existing code (a test data file). It adds no script, no scheduler or pull-request hook, no long-running supervisor and no database work. Nothing needs an entry in `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`.

## Files likely to change
- `tests/e2e_smoke_canary_b.txt` (created if it does not exist, edited if it does)

## Functions or modules to implement
None. This is a data-file edit only.
- If the file is missing, create it with exactly two lines: `status: ok`, then `decompose-run: 39879064171`, ending with one trailing newline.
- If the file exists, replace line 1 with `status: ok` and make line 2 `decompose-run: 39879064171`. If line 2 already exists, replace it in place; if it does not, insert it. Leave every later line as it is.
- In both cases the file ends with exactly one trailing newline.

## Data structures affected
Only the plain-text canary file.

## API or interface changes
None.

## Decisions
### D1 — Replace line 2 in place rather than insert a new line
- Chosen: overwrite the existing second line, or add it if the file has only one line.
- Alternatives considered: insert a new line 2 and push the existing content down.
- Why: the issue says to "make the second line" the given value, and overwriting means a rerun leaves the same result (idempotent) without adding duplicate lines.

## Security considerations
- No trust boundary, endpoint, credential or money handling is involved.
- The values written are fixed literals, so there is no outside input to validate.
- The only abuse case is editing the wrong file. The scope rule below rules it out: only `tests/e2e_smoke_canary_b.txt` may change, and the sibling's `tests/e2e_smoke_canary.txt` must not.

## Risks and edge cases
- The sibling issue edits `tests/e2e_smoke_canary.txt` in parallel. Because each issue touches a different path, the two cannot conflict.
- A file with a missing trailing newline, or with CRLF line endings, must end up with exactly one LF trailing newline.
- Do not reflow or reformat any content after line 2.

## Testing considerations
Run these checks after the change:
- `head -n1 tests/e2e_smoke_canary_b.txt` prints `status: ok`.
- `sed -n 2p tests/e2e_smoke_canary_b.txt` prints `decompose-run: 39879064171`.
- `tail -c1` on the file shows a newline.
- `git diff --stat` lists only `tests/e2e_smoke_canary_b.txt`.

No changelog or `agents.d` fragment is needed, because there is no behaviour change.
